new_entities.name: Citicoline (CDP-choline)
new_entities.description: An orally administered choline donor used to support membrane phospholipid synthesis and cognitive function.

new_entities.name: Memory decline related to aging
new_entities.description: Declining memory performance in older adults without overt dementia or with mild chronic cerebral impairment.

edges.population: older adults with age-associated memory impairment or chronic cerebral cognitive decline
edges.mechanism: Citicoline supplies choline and cytidine needed for phosphatidylcholine synthesis and acetylcholine support, which may help neuronal membrane turnover and memory-related neurotransmission in aging brains. Human benefits appear more plausible in people with baseline inefficiency or impairment than in already high-functioning younger adults.
edges.summary: Citicoline has a modest but plausible evidence base for supporting memory in older adults with age-related decline. The newer placebo-controlled trial in age-associated memory impairment is positive, and older randomized evidence plus Cochrane review data point in the same general direction, though the literature is older and methodologically uneven.
edges.caveats: Much of the evidence predates modern trial standards and often mixes age-related decline with broader chronic cerebrovascular cognitive impairment. The overall signal looks more like a modest niche benefit than a dramatic memory-restoring effect.

evidence.citation: Nakazaki E et al 2021 J Nutr
evidence.notes: Citicoline and Memory Function in Healthy Older Adults: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial.
